query: How can we improve incident resolution efficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident is a common cause of both how it is handled (resolution action) and how efficiently it resolves; not a lever an actor sets, and not named in the query.

per_column.name: affected_device_type
per_column.rationale: Device type influences both the resolution approach chosen and the difficulty/speed of resolution; an intrinsic property of the incident, not intervenable, not named.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity affects both the action taken and the time to resolve; it is a characteristic of the fault, not a settable lever, and not named.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: The resolution action (repair, replace, configure, investigate) is something an operator could actually choose or change, making it an intervenable treatment on the efficiency outcome.

per_column.name: reassignment_flag
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident is reassigned is an operational decision that can be set/changed, and it plausibly affects resolution efficiency; a valid intervenable lever.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident recurs reflects underlying problem difficulty that drives both handling and speed; not directly settable, not named.

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency of the disruption is a property of the incident that shapes both prioritization/action and resolution time; not an intervenable lever, not named.

per_column.name: repeat_caller_flag
per_column.rationale: Constant value (all true) carries no variation, so it cannot function as treatment, confounder, or informative covariate.

judge.rationale: The query poses a genuinely interventional 'how can we improve' question about resolution efficiency. At least two added columns (resolution_action_type, reassignment_flag) are genuinely intervenable treatments an actor can set, satisfying condition (a). Several columns (incident_category, affected_device_type, failure_symptom_severity, urgency_signal, repeat_incident_signal) are plausible common causes of both the chosen action and the resolution speed, and none are named in the vague query, demonstrating the confounder-generation capability under test. One column (repeat_caller_flag) is a constant and contributes nothing. Overall the set realises the what-if claim with reasonably strong, unnamed confounders.
